messages.content:
You are a helpful writing assistant. You help professionals draft clear,
effective workplace communication.

I have to tell my manager I'm going to miss the Friday deadline on the
migration. It's my fault - I underestimated it. I want to say it straight
without it turning into a whole thing. Can you help me word it?

Here are two clean, low-drama options. Pick the one that matches your usual channel.

**Email version**
Subject: Timeline update: [Migration/Project Name]
Hi [Manager],
I’m writing to let you know I won’t be able to finish the migration by Friday. I underestimated the scope, and I take responsibility for that. Based on current progress, I can complete it by [new date/time]. I’m prioritizing it now and will share a quick status update on [day]. If this impacts anything downstream, let me know and I’ll adjust priorities accordingly.
Best,
[Your Name]

**Slack/IM version**
Hi [Manager] – quick update: I won’t make the Friday deadline on the migration. I underestimated the work, and I own that. I can have it done by [new date/time] instead. I’m focusing on it now and will keep you posted. Flag any downstream impacts and I’ll adjust accordingly. Thanks!

**A few tips to keep it from turning into a "whole thing":**
- Send it as soon as you know. Early notice shows respect for their planning.
- Don’t over-apologize or over-explain. One clear sentence of ownership is enough.
- Give a specific, realistic new deadline you’re confident you can hit.
- Be ready to briefly answer follow-ups, then pivot back to execution.

Want me to tailor it to your exact project name, new date, or company tone? Just share those details.

thanks yeah i like the email one but feels kinda formal? we usually just text casually. also "i take responsibility for that" is a bit much lol. can you trim it down but still own it? new deadline would be tuesday btw

Here’s a trimmed, casual version you can drop straight into Slack or text:

> Hey [Manager], quick update on the migration: I won’t make Friday. I underestimated the work, and I’m sorry about the delay. I can have it done by Tuesday instead. I’m focused on it now and will keep you posted. If this affects anything else on your plate, just say the word and I’ll shift priorities. Thanks!

**Why this works:**
- Opens with the news immediately (no fluff)
- Owns it lightly without over-apologizing or sounding stiff
- Gives a concrete new deadline
- Shows you’re already handling it and leaves room for course-correction if needed

Send it early in the day so your manager can adjust plans before the week winds down. Want it tweaked to match your exact project name or usual sign-off? Just say the word.
ok yeah thats way better. should i mention why i underestimated or just leave it? like hes def gonna ask what's left to finish so idk if i should get ahead of it or just wait

Skip the deep "why" for now. Your manager will likely ask, but you can front-load a quick **"what's left"** instead. That keeps it casual, shows you're in control, and usually stops the follow-up.

Try this:

> Hey [Manager], quick update on the migration: I won’t make Friday. I underestimated the work, and I’m sorry about the delay. I can have it done by Tuesday instead. The last piece is [e.g., data validation / final testing / the staging server], and I’m wrapping it up now. I’ll keep you posted. If this affects anything else on your plate, just say the word and I’ll shift priorities. Thanks!

**Why this works:**
- Answers the inevitable "what's left?" before they have to ask
- Keeps the root-cause conversation out of it (no over-explaining, no defensiveness)
- Stays casual and forward-looking

If your manager is super hands-off, you can even drop the bracketed part and just say `"I'm wrapping up the final pieces now."` If they like visibility, that one-line status update will save you a follow-up message and keep things moving.

Want me to slot in the exact remaining task? Just tell me what’s left and I’ll tighten it up.
